findings.finding: Claim under doubt: Anchoring `.shipwright/agent_docs/iterates/` entries to `<run_id>.json` / `<run_id>.test-results.json` (with `run_id` matching `RUN_ID_STRICT`, already enforced at write time by `iterate_entry.py`/`iterate_test_results.py`) closes the same class of gap Round 4 closed for `reviews.json`, making it safe to keep skip-safe. — `RUN_ID_STRICT` is a public, freely-choosable filename shape, not a signature — a contributor's own PR can commit a brand-new, self-authored, shape-valid file under this prefix carrying forged content; nothing about the write-time enforcement of that shape by the legitimate producer prevents an attacker from independently producing a file matching the same shape. A concrete real consumer trusts that content unauthenticated: `plugins/shipwright-iterate/scripts/lib/complexity_history.py::load_history_prior` globs every `*.json` directly under this dir and accepts any file with a valid `complexity` + parseable `date`, feeding it into later iterates' complexity default (`prior_source: history`) with zero authorship or provenance check. The claim conflated 'shape enforced at write time by the legitimate producer' with 'shape can only be produced by the legitimate producer' — Round 4 already showed those are not the same thing for `reviews.json`, and this anchor repeated exactly that mistake one directory over. Disproved.
findings.suggestion: Either (a) apply the same treatment given to `.shipwright/compliance/` — remove `.shipwright/agent_docs/iterates/` from skip-safety entirely now that a concrete downstream truster (`complexity_history.load_history_prior`) is identified, accepting one extra trivial review call for iterate-record-only PRs, or (b) disclose this explicitly as an accepted residual risk.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: The comment comparing the `CHANGELOG-unreleased.d/` wildcard's residual risk to the `external-*review*` hide-side wildcard treats the two as comparably low-stakes: both are described as leaving a shape-conforming but content-forged file 'hidden from one review call'. — The two are not comparable. `external-*review*` is hide-only: even a forged file under that prefix still leaves the rest of the diff subject to a real model review, so it is hidden from one review call within an otherwise-reviewed PR. `CHANGELOG-unreleased.d/` is hidden AND skip-safe, so a PR whose only change is one shape-conforming drop gets zero review, human or model, not merely one hidden section. The comment's wording obscured this asymmetry.
findings.suggestion: Reword the comment to state explicitly that a matching CHANGELOG-only PR gets zero review, and ground the acceptance in the absence of any content-trusting downstream reader for that prefix (drops are aggregated into CHANGELOG.md by a human-run `/shipwright-changelog`, never consumed as a gate oracle) rather than implying parity with the hide-side wildcard's residual risk.

findings.finding: The anchor assumes the producer's counter is always exactly three zero-padded digits. If `write_changelog_drop._next_counter_path` ever emits a 4-digit counter (a category with ≥1000 drops, or if padding is configurable), a legitimate drop would silently lose skip-safety. This fails safe (extra trivial review), not open, but the sync constraint with the producer isn't enforced or tested at a shared constant.
findings.suggestion: Either import/derive the pattern from `write_changelog_drop` (or assert sync in a test that reads the producer's `_next_counter_path` output format), or relax to `\d{3,}`.

findings.finding: is_safe_to_skip_review` was removed entirely from `pr_review_generated.py`. Only `review_record_tier.py` and the test file are updated in this diff; any other consumer importing it from the old module (none visible here, but the diff doesn't prove the repo-wide caller set) would break with an ImportError.
findings.suggestion: A grep of the repo for `from pr_review_generated import`/`pr_review_generated.is_safe_to_skip_review` should be recorded as verified; the self-review claims this was checked ("sole caller confirmed") but the diff itself carries no evidence. If any external plugin re-exports it, add a shim.

findings.finding: The positive tests only cover `Fixed/` and `Security/` categories with counters `001` and `012`; there is no test that a category segment with trailing/leading whitespace or an attacker category that happens to be one of the six after unicode normalization is rejected. Minor — the closed frozenset comparison is exact — but the category check could also be exercised against a category that is a real name with trailing slash-less suffix like `Fixed2`, which the regex/`not in` set correctly rejects; that axis is untested.
findings.suggestion: Add `Fixed2/...` and a real-category-with-trailing-space case to the negative test.  Everything material in the spec is implemented and verifiable in the diff: compliance/, iterates/, runtime/ removed from skip-safety; CHANGELOG-unreleased.d/ anchored to the six-category + `_<NNN>.md` shape; the zero-review disclosure rewording present in the PER-PREFIX comment; `is_generated_path` (hide side) untouched; sole visible caller `review_record_tier.py` import updated; tests assert both the hide-side preservation and the skip-side removal for each dropped prefix, and isolate single failure axes for the changelog anchor. No security regression introduced — the change strictly narrows the skip-gate.  Overall assessment: ship-as-is; findings are hardening refinements, none block.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: approve

findings.finding: strip()` turns a real Git path with leading or trailing whitespace into a canonical changelog-drop path. For example, ` CHANGELOG-unreleased.d/Fixed/x_001.md` would be allowed to make a PR skip review, despite not matching the required repo path shape.
findings.suggestion: Do not normalize the path in this security classifier (`p = path or ""`); preserve exact path bytes and reject whitespace-prefixed/suffixed lookalikes. Add negative tests for both cases.  Ship-with-fixes: the per-prefix decisions otherwise match the specification, but the new canonical-path check is bypassable for valid Git filenames containing boundary whitespace.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
